new_assertions.body: The current tested scalar coordinate is count-aware and role-aware: ZOE count state is attached to a component identity built from frontier-relative residual incidence plus support-capacity parity aligned to incidence column roles.

Support height matters to scalar value through its relation to residual role, not merely through total or unordered capacity; one aligned parity bit per local column is sufficient on the current derivation corpus and fresh 6x3-k4.
The fresh 6x3-k4 result is a strict Q-V compression: ROLE_CAPPAR merges exact-type ZOE classes while preserving scalar purity on a carrier where the affine parity model fails.

The earlier two-syndrome result was conditional on a binary component-parity coordinate that is now known to be information-incomplete on 4x5-k4; decoder discovery must therefore be re-derived in the repaired ROLE_CAPPAR+ZOE coordinate rather than transplanted unchanged.
Decoder discovery should first measure the value target dimension relative to the frozen ROLE_CAPPAR+ZOE coordinate and simple structural projections before fitting any coefficients.
A decoder candidate must be frozen structurally before outcome qualification and tested on at least one carrier not used to choose its formula; exact class lookup is a control, not a final law.
